stem:
Omkar asks whether $47$ can be a perfect square.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call $47$ a perfect-square label without testing its digits.
Say being a perfect square is what produces a forbidden units digit, reversing the digit test.
No: a perfect square cannot end in $7$, so $47$ is not a perfect square.
Reject $47$ only because the printed tens digit $4$ looks even.

teacher.key_rationale: Possible units digits of perfect squares never include $2$, $3$, $7$, or $8$. Ending in $7$ rules $47$ out. Relabelling without the test, reversing the implication, or judging by the tens digit alone all miss that units-digit filter.
